clauses.reason: Paragraph 1 authorises the Administrator of Veterans' Affairs to pay actual necessary travel expenses (lodging and subsistence included) of claimants and beneficiaries traveling under prior authorization. Paragraph 5 of EO 9975 (13 FR 3805) provides "This order supersedes Executive Order No. 9446 of June 8, 1944", and EO 9975 states no later effective date, so the supersession took effect on signing, 1948-07-07 (actor: President Truman).

Paragraph 2 authorises payment of 3 cents per mile in lieu of actual expenses. Paragraph 5 of EO 9975 (13 FR 3805) provides "This order supersedes Executive Order No. 9446 of June 8, 1944", and EO 9975 states no later effective date, so the supersession took effect on signing, 1948-07-07 (actor: President Truman).

Paragraph 3 allows payment of the allowance upon termination of examination, treatment or care and before completion of travel. Paragraph 5 of EO 9975 (13 FR 3805) provides "This order supersedes Executive Order No. 9446 of June 8, 1944", and EO 9975 states no later effective date, so the supersession took effect on signing, 1948-07-07 (actor: President Truman).

Paragraph 4 extends the same basis of travel expenses to attendants who are not Veterans' Administration employees. Paragraph 5 of EO 9975 (13 FR 3805) provides "This order supersedes Executive Order No. 9446 of June 8, 1944", and EO 9975 states no later effective date, so the supersession took effect on signing, 1948-07-07 (actor: President Truman).

Paragraph 5 lets the Administrator prescribe rules and regulations not inconsistent with the order. Paragraph 5 of EO 9975 (13 FR 3805) provides "This order supersedes Executive Order No. 9446 of June 8, 1944", and EO 9975 states no later effective date, so the supersession took effect on signing, 1948-07-07 (actor: President Truman).

research_rationale:
EO 9446 (signed 1944-06-08, effective 1944-07-01 by its own terms; 9 FR 6293) prescribed five paragraphs of regulations on travel-expense allowances for Veterans' Administration claimants, beneficiaries and attendants under the act of March 14, 1940 (54 Stat. 49). Paragraph 5 of EO 9975 (signed 1948-07-07; 13 FR 3805, held in the Federal Register printing) states "This order supersedes Executive Order No. 9446 of June 8, 1944" and re-prescribes regulations on the same subject. EO 9975 states no later effective date, so it took effect on signing, 1948-07-07; all five clauses of EO 9446 ended then by express supersession. A search of the held texts for the number 9446 finds only EO 9975 (and a duplicate printing page) as later instruments; the dossier chain records the single supersession. Status proposal: no.
